draft.title: Simple, compound and complex sentences
card: A clause is a group of words with a verb. A main clause makes sense on its own. A dependent clause does not make sense on its own.
one main clause. Example: Mia kicked the ball.
two main clauses joined by a word such as and, but or so. Example: Mia kicked the ball, and Sam caught it.
a main clause plus a dependent clause that starts with a word such as because, when or although. Example: Sam caught the ball because he was ready.
draft.remember: Count the main clauses, then look for a dependent clause that cannot stand alone.

a.q: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
opts: Leo packed his bag when the bell rang
Leo packed his bag and he left the room
Leo packed his bag quickly and quietly
Leo packed his bag, but Ana stayed behind
a.why: The words when the bell rang are a dependent clause. They need the main clause to make sense. The option with but joins two main clauses, so it is compound, not complex.
a.clue: Look for a group of words that cannot stand alone.

b.q: Which describes this sentence? The storm hit Darwin, but the school stayed open.
opts: Compound, with two main clauses joined by but
Complex, with a dependent clause starting with but
Simple, with one main clause and two nouns
Complex, with a dependent clause about the school
b.why: The storm hit Darwin and the school stayed open could each stand alone, and but joins them. That makes two main clauses, so it is compound. A joining word does not always start a dependent clause.
b.clue: Test whether each half could be a sentence by itself.

a.best: Leo packed his bag when the bell rang

b.best: Compound, with two main clauses joined by but
